newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Coceral sees rise in EU voluntary set-aside.
newsitem.headline: Coceral sees rise in EU voluntary set-aside.

text.p: A lower than expected cereals area forecast for the 1997 harvest suggests an increase in voluntary set-aside, Coceral, the EU grain trade lobby said.
In minutes of a recent meeting of the EU cereals advisory committee, Coceral added that drought in Spain could lead to additional last minute drillings of sunflower seed.
The farmers and traders agreed to meet at the end of May or early June to advise the European Commission on the compulsory set-aside rate for the 1998 harvest.
Last Monday French Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur called for set-aside to be reduced to zero from five percent to keep exports flowing, and for the rate to be fixed by June 30, 1997.
On Thursday, the EU imposed a tax on daily wheat and flour exports to save stocks for domestic consumers and hold down rising prices.
On April 18, Coceral forecast a 2.2 percent increase in the EU grain area to 37.09 million hectares despite a halving of the set-aside rate to five percent in 1997.
COPA, the EU farmers' body, has forecast a 2.0 percent rise to 37.65 million ha but warned that weather would be an major factor in production.
The farmers saw higher wheat and barley sowings than the grain traders.
Soft wheat sowings were seen rising to 14.06 million ha in 1997 from 13.78 million in 1996 and the barley area to 11.78 million ha from 11.39 million.
The maize area was put slightly lower at 4.16 million ha against 4.19 million in 1996. Coceral put 1997 maize area 0.9 percent higher at 4.11 million ha.
